paper.title_en: Interacting Barrow-generalised Ricci holographic dark energy in f(Q,T) Bianchi-I cosmology: observational constraints versus classical stability
paper.abstract_en: We study an interacting Barrow-generalized Ricci holographic dark-energy (BGRHDE) model in f(Q,T)=Q+\alpha Q^{2}+\beta T gravity on a locally rotationally symmetric Bianchi type-I background. The dark-energy density is built from a Granda-Oliveros infrared cut-off deformed by the Barrow entropy exponent and is allowed to exchange energy with pressureless matter. Rather than prescribing the scale factor, we fix the expansion history through the single-variable deceleration law q=b-\nu /H, which integrates in closed form and renders every geometric and dark-sector quantity an explicit function of redshift. The model describes a smooth transition to acceleration with a de Sitter attractor and a frozen, subdominant anisotropy, the strong energy condition being violated only in the accelerating era. A joint Markov-chain Monte Carlo fit to cosmic-chronometer, Pantheon+ supernova and DESI DR2 baryon-acoustic-oscillation data yields H_{0}=68.1\pm 1.5\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}}, b=0.84\pm 0.04, q_{0}=-0.44\pm 0.02 and a transition at z_{t}=0.73\pm 0.02, with a sound horizon consistent with Planck and an information-criterion comparison that leaves the model competitive with \Lambda \text{CDM}. The data-preferred parameters and the region of classical sound-speed stability, which requires b\gtrsim 1.8, are found to be disjoint, quantifying within a specific anisotropic framework a tension between observational viability and perturbative stability that is generic to holographic dark energy. Because the reconstruction is analytic and its internal consistency is monitored throughout by a second-Friedmann residual, the framework provides a transparent testbed for confronting holographic dark energy with current expansion-rate data.
